result:
Two findings, handled differently.

**Minor (typo):** a valid docstring fix, and there's nothing to test-drive. I'll make it.

**Important (HALF_UP):** I'm declining this one. D2 is the owner's recorded decision from plan review: round half-even to match the ledger system. The spec is the binding authority, and the reviewer's "customers expect half-up" is an unsupported claim that contradicts it. D2 isn't a scope fence, and none of the five stops applies. So this is a ledgered ruling, not a stall. If the ruling is wrong, the cost is a one-line constant change plus a test.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

<command>
make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/fix-pass-test.log 2>&1; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/fix-pass-test.log
</command>

If the tests pass, I commit the fix and append the ruling to the ledger in the same call:

<command>
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "docs: fix typo in round_price docstring" && printf '%s\n' "Final review: Minor (docstring typo 'neerest') fixed; tests: make test -> pass" "Ruling: Declined reviewer's switch to ROUND_HALF_UP; kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN — plan Decision D2 (owner, plan review, 2026-11-02) fixes half-even to match the ledger system, and the reviewer cites no spec basis for half-up — if wrong, exact half-cent ties price one cent lower than customers expect; the fix is one constant plus a test." >> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md
</command>

I then continue with the plan-completion protocol and finishing-a-development-branch. The merge or push is a stop, so I'd ask before doing it.

**Message to partner:**

> The rate-card plan is complete: every task is done and `make test` passes. The final whole-plan review returned two findings.
>
> 1. **Fixed:** the docstring typo "neerest" in `round_price()`. Tests still pass.
> 2. **Declined, needs your attention:** the reviewer said `round_price()` should use ROUND_HALF_UP because "customers expect half-up." The plan's Decision D2 (yours, from plan review on 2026-11-02) says half-even, to match the ledger system, so I kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN. The reviewer gave no spec basis for half-up, and I didn't reopen your decision. I recorded this as a `Ruling:` in the ledger.
>
> If customer-facing prices really should round half-up, that's a product call that overrides D2. It would be a one-line change in `rates/card.py` plus a test for tie cases, and it would then no longer match the ledger system. Tell me if you want it.
>
> I'm stopping at the plan-completion gate. Merging or pushing the branch is yours to approve.
